purpose: Candidate retrieval, scoped feature lookup, and concept-graph membership. LLM review decides identity and applicability.

object.definition: There are $K$ arms with rewards in $[0,1]$, independent across rounds. All reward laws and unknown means $\mu_{t,i}$ are fixed before interaction. Total mean drift is $$V_\mu=\sum_{t=2}^{T}\|\mu_t-\mu_{t-1}\|_\infty,\qquad \mu_t=(\mu_{t,1},\ldots,\mu_{t,K}).$$.

operation.display_label_zh: Scalar reward of the selected action
operation.query_signature: Choose arm $I_t$, then receive only its reward. Inputs $K,T$ are public; $V_\mu$, means, and change locations are hidden, and no nontrivial actual-drift bound is given. A single causal policy cannot take $V_\mu$ or a nontrivial bound on it as input. Past feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no additional historical or sample queries are available beyond the explicitly declared interface.

steps: Each round selects one arm $I_t$ and receives only that arm's reward.
The data $K,T$ are public. The quantity $V_\mu$, means, and change locations are hidden. No nontrivial upper bound on actual drift is supplied.
The common causal policy may use neither $V_\mu$ nor a nontrivial upper bound on it as input.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.
